items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: he was staying on the South Side, and he said, now you just lay here and we've got to do a couple of promotions and we're going down to see Marty Pay and Daddy O' Dayley down at the studio, and we're gonna publicize these events.

ctx.x: Well, we went to Western Union and it arrived, and he said come on, and we went down to this ... it wasn't a hotel; it was this new high rise down there on Houston, right off of West Broadway; he was staying with some friends. We stayed there all night until it was plane time the next morning, so I came back to Chicago. I had left Chicago in '56, and here I'm on my way back to play some concerts, and I felt that it was pretty good, as I had a chance to see my mother and grandmother and son and what not.

So we arrived and he took me out to his house and he was staying on the South Side, and he said, now you just lay here and we've got to do a couple of promotions and we're going down to see Marty Pay and Daddy O' Dayley down at the studio, and we're gonna publicize these events. And he put signs up

all around the South Side and the North Side of Chicago.
So I'm making contact with all those folks, you know, everybody that hadn't seen me, since I made my big debut in New York; however, I didn't have a fiddle, naturally. I got rid of the fiddle that I did have, and an old army buddy of mine, Karl Ervin -- Smitty we used to call him in the service; a young fellow, he needed money then, and called on him and he wanted to know what was happening, and he said; "Got a fiddle?
